definitions.explanation: A general term referring to various things, situations, or matters.
Used to refer to things in general, often in philosophical or abstract contexts.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}を{考|かんが}える。
{物事|ものごと}を{前向|まえむ}きに{考|かんが}える。
{物事|ものごと}の{見方|みかた}は{人|ひと}によって{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: The way of looking at things differs depending on the person.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{物事|ものごと}を{深|ふか}く{考|かんが}えるタイプだ。
examples.english: He is the type who thinks deeply about things.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}を{始|はじ}める{前|まえ}に、よく{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Before starting anything, it is important to make a good plan.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}には{順序|じゅんじょ}がある。
examples.english: There is an order to things.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}の{本質|ほんしつ}を{見抜|みぬ}く。
examples.english: To see through to the essence of things.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}には{表|おもて}と{裏|うら}がある。
あまり{物事|ものごと}を{難|むずか}しく{考|かんが}えないほうがいい。
examples.english: You shouldn't think about things too seriously.

examples.japanese: {物事|ものごと}を{客観的|きゃっかんてき}に{見|み}ることができれば、{正|ただ}しい{判断|はんだん}ができるようになる。
examples.english: If you can view things objectively, you will be able to make correct judgments.

notes:
{物事|ものごと} is a general noun referring to "things" in an abstract sense—matters, affairs, or phenomena.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {物事|ものごと}を{考|かんが}える (to think about things)
- {物事|ものごと}の{見方|みかた} (perspective on things)
- {物事|ものごと}の{順序|じゅんじょ} (order of things)
- {物事|ものごと}に{対|たい}する{態度|たいど} (attitude toward things)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {物事|ものごと} vs. もの: もの refers to concrete objects or abstract concepts ("thing"); {物事|ものごと} specifically refers to matters, affairs, or issues.
- {物事|ものごと} vs. こと: こと means "thing" in the sense of events or matters; {物事|ものごと} is more comprehensive and often used in set expressions.

USAGE:
{物事|ものごと} is often used in expressions about one's approach to life, philosophy, or general attitude. It has a somewhat formal or contemplative nuance.
